items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1975-02-19
items.q: I've known, for example, Jeanette Kimball, who plays the piano in Papa Celestan's band. I've known her since I was five years old.

ctx.x: That's right, yeah. Because, well, there was nothing else to take. And all those... See, there are a lot of musicians that the family just hired from time to time, like to go out to Millenburg for a picnic. I mean, we'd hire Papa Celestan's band, you know. And so I knew all the musicians. I've known, for example, Jeanette Kimball, who plays the piano in Papa Celestan's band. I've known her since I was five years old. And so, you know, having grown up with a musician like that, I mean, a musician was never…

It seems to me that, you know, in a sense you're in a class of people. When I put Hammond in with you, to a certain extent you may disagree with me. But these people, like yourself and Hammond, that started producing jazz concerts, were also interested in record collecting, or maybe, you know, or at least had a lot of records.

items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1975-02-03
items.q: And we have, of course, Armand Hug and Jeanette Kimball who can play the piano for these purposes... Jeanette Kimball on piano

ctx.x: Well we can still manage with trombone and cornet though. There are still some trombone and cornet players. But clarinet players who can play the harmonic role of a clarinet in a jazz band, we don't have. As you recall we found that Eddie Miller was in shape to play clarinet last time, and he hadn't played in thirty years, but he broke out his clarinet and we did make a session. And I don't know what we're going to do exactly next time. I have some plans, enough to cut four more sessions. But we only have the two…
and we could use them to play the piano for each session. Well there's a young stuff that plays right, Dan.
